name: TX-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Craig Goldman renominated and heavily funded ($1.5M cash)
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~94%
No public polling of the general election
model.rationale: Goldman holds a seat with an R+11 lean, enters with a large fundraising edge and no outside opposition spending, and markets give him roughly a 94% chance. With no polls and a little-known Democratic challenger, the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin of about R+15.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing the challenger within single digits, or a major scandal or redistricting change, would warrant moving this race toward tossup territory.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-12 is a solidly Republican Fort Worth–area seat, and first-term incumbent Craig Goldman is running for reelection after clearing his primary. He has raised about $1.8 million and holds a $1.5 million war chest, with no recorded outside spending against him. Democratic challenger Angela Rodriguez Prilliman has no reported fundraising totals, leaving a large resource gap.

No public general-election polls cover the race, and no expert raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on the district's R+11 partisan lean, the incumbent's financial advantage, and prediction markets that price a Republican win at about 94%. The expected margin is roughly fifteen points Republican, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling.
